title: Architecture, peinture et sculpture de la maison de ville d'Amsterdam, représentée en CIX figures en taille-douce ...
shelf_note: A 1719 French description of the Amsterdam Town Hall's sculpture, plate by plate. The leaf matches the title and the language. No tradition or collection is assigned, so there is nothing for it to contradict.
structure_note: The image is an unsplit opening showing printed pp. 18 and 19. The OCR transcribes both pages in order as two blocks, with `<page-num>18` and `<page-num>19`, which is the deliberate-opening handling and not a lost half. If the whole book is scanned as openings, one record holds two printed numbers, so with_printed_number at 16/169 and the 4 backsteps and 2 repeats more likely come from that two-numbers-per-record pattern or numeral misreads than from a misordered scan. Neither can be confirmed from one page. structure.pages_translated is 0 while the book field says 127 (and this page carries a translation), so one of the counters is wrong (E2).

other.note: Raw `<column-break/>` appears twice in the English payload, and `<header>`/`<sig>E 2</sig>` sit mid-text between the two printed pages. Unless the renderer strips them, a reader sees markup in the text.

The continuity meta '<meta>continues from previous page: description of the ornaments of the Pedestal of Mercury</meta>' names a 'Pedestal of Mercury' that this leaf does not mention. The leaf names only 'ce Dieu' with caduceus, winged hat and purse, so Mercury is a fair inference but 'Pedestal' is not shown here.

book_verdict: The transcription and translation of this 1719 opening are faithful and the notes are accurate and helpful. The note on 'Diane' versus Dione flags a real slip in the source instead of hiding it. The only on-sight blemish is raw layout markup (`<column-break/>`, `<sig>`) left in the English, plus a counter mismatch in the book's structure fields.
